name.text: Which pairs satisfy an inequality in two unknowns

questiontext.text:
For the inequality {@id@}, decide for each pair \((x, y)\) whether the inequality is true.

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
A pair \((x, y)\) is a solution when it makes the inequality true. Work out the left side, compare it with \({@c@}\), and remember that [[if test="strictp(rel)"]]this strict sign does not allow the two sides to be equal[[else]]this sign allows the two sides to be equal[[/if]].

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\): \({@a@}({@P[1][1]@}) + {@b@}({@P[1][2]@}) = {@val[1]@}\). [[if test="is(cats[1]=1)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), and the sign allows equal: true.[[elif test="is(cats[1]=2)"]]\({@val[1]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is true.[[elif test="is(val[1]=c)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), but the sign does not allow equal: false.[[else]]\({@val[1]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is false.[[/if]]

  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\): \({@a@}({@P[2][1]@}) + {@b@}({@P[2][2]@}) = {@val[2]@}\). [[if test="is(cats[2]=1)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), and the sign allows equal: true.[[elif test="is(cats[2]=2)"]]\({@val[2]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is true.[[elif test="is(val[2]=c)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), but the sign does not allow equal: false.[[else]]\({@val[2]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is false.[[/if]]

  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\): \({@a@}({@P[3][1]@}) + {@b@}({@P[3][2]@}) = {@val[3]@}\). [[if test="is(cats[3]=1)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), and the sign allows equal: true.[[elif test="is(cats[3]=2)"]]\({@val[3]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is true.[[elif test="is(val[3]=c)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), but the sign does not allow equal: false.[[else]]\({@val[3]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is false.[[/if]]

  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\): \({@a@}({@P[4][1]@}) + {@b@}({@P[4][2]@}) = {@val[4]@}\). [[if test="is(cats[4]=1)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), and the sign allows equal: true.[[elif test="is(cats[4]=2)"]]\({@val[4]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is true.[[elif test="is(val[4]=c)"]]Both sides equal \({@c@}\), but the sign does not allow equal: false.[[else]]\({@val[4]@} {@relt(rel)@} {@c@}\) is false.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: which pairs satisfy an inequality in two unknowns

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Decide whether pairs satisfy a linear inequality in two unknowns, including a pair on the boundary.

Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).
